title: Strands autologging with a shared OpenTelemetry provider: spans without an MLflow request ID are skipped, not registered
answers: Why does mlflow.strands.autolog raise KeyError(None) when my app also sends OpenTelemetry spans?
Strands tracing with a shared tracer provider: how are spans from other instrumentation handled?
Where is the Strands span processor's on_start deciding whether a span belongs to MLflow tracing?
How do I make a new span processor ignore child spans that MLflow's base processor did not tag with a request ID?
body:
Path: mlflow/strands/autolog.py:on_start is the Strands span processor hook that runs for every OpenTelemetry span started while mlflow.strands.autolog() is enabled, including spans from other instrumentation when MLflow shares a global tracer provider (MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER=false).
Rule: After the base processor runs, read the request ID with get_otel_attribute(span, SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID) and return early when it is None, before create_mlflow_span and InMemoryTraceManager.register_span. Foreign spans then stay outside MLflow tracing. Apply the same guard in any MLflow span processor that registers spans after delegating to a base processor.
Symptom: With a shared provider, starting an unrelated span (for example a remote-parent server span) raised KeyError(None) from the Strands autolog path, because the base processor had skipped the span and left no request ID to register it under.
Constraints: Applies to spans whose request ID is missing after the base processor has run. Does not change how spans that do carry a request ID are created or registered. Regression coverage is test_strands_autolog_shared_provider_skips_foreign_span in tests/strands/test_strands_tracing.py, which asserts no traces are produced.
applies: Strands autologging (mlflow.strands.autolog) when MLflow shares an OpenTelemetry tracer provider with other instrumentation.
says: Strands automatic logging crashes with a key error when the application emits external tracing spans.
Strands tracing should safely ignore foreign OpenTelemetry spans when using a shared tracer provider.
Starting third-party tracing spans causes Strands autologging to crash with missing request identifiers.
search: In mlflow/strands/autolog.py:on_start, inspect get_otel_attribute(span, SpanAttributeKey.REQUEST_ID) after the base processor runs and return early if it is None, before calling create_mlflow_span and InMemoryTraceManager.register_span. This guard ensures foreign OpenTelemetry spans from a shared tracer provider (MLFLOW_USE_DEFAULT_TRACER_PROVIDER=false) are excluded from MLflow tracing instead of raising KeyError(None). The same early-return check should be applied to any MLflow span processor that registers spans after delegating to a base processor. The rule applies only to spans missing a request ID and is verified by test_strands_autolog_shared_provider_skips_foreign_span.
